verdict: Carvana sold a record 217,385 cars and grew revenue 42% to $8.04B, keeping $483M of consolidated profit even after a $53M charge for paying off debt early.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Per Class A share; net income attributable to Carvana Co. was $289M (see note below on the $483M consolidated figure)

kpis.label: Retail units sold
kpis.note: +39% YoY — the first quarter over 200,000 cars, while the wider market was roughly flat

kpis.label: Operating income
kpis.note: A record; an 8.9% operating margin, down from 9.8% a year ago

segments.name: Retail vehicle sales
segments.note: Used cars sold to individual buyers online — the core business. Retail units sold hit a record 217,385, up 39%.

segments.name: Wholesale sales and revenues
segments.note: Cars sold on to other dealers, including through Carvana's wholesale marketplace (the ADESA business).

segments.name: Other sales and revenues
segments.note: Everything else — mainly gains on selling the car loans it makes to buyers, plus vehicle service contracts and other add-ons.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Running the business: staff pay ($255M), advertising ($152M), logistics ($68M), market occupancy ($18M) and $312M of other costs (IT, insurance, warranty and registration costs).

opex.name: Other operating expense
opex.note: Small net operating costs, mainly gains and losses on disposing of buildings and equipment.

otherDetail: Other expense was $162M, net: $98M of interest expense, net (interest on its notes, loans and car-financing facilities, after interest earned on cash), a $53M loss on debt extinguishment (paying off debt early — see one-off items), and $11M of other expense, net — mainly warrant-related charges from the 2026 Warrant Exchange and a $5M fall in the value of new warrants, partly offset by a $7M rise in the value of its stakes in loan securitizations (bundles of car loans sold to investors).
follow100Note: The $483M kept as profit is Carvana's consolidated net income. Of that, $194M belongs to noncontrolling interests — the other owners of Carvana Group, LLC — leaving $289M attributable to Carvana Co. shareholders, which is the figure behind the $0.39 diluted EPS.

takeaways.title: Record cars sold, taking share
takeaways.text: Retail units sold rose 39% to a record 217,385 — the eighth straight quarter of roughly 40% growth — while the wider used-car market was roughly flat. Retail vehicle revenue jumped 54% to $6.14B and total revenue rose 42% to a record $8.04B.

takeaways.title: Each car earned a little less
takeaways.text: Gross profit rose 32% to $1.52B, but gross profit per unit fell $365 to $6,997. Carvana chose to pass value back to buyers through cheaper loan rates, wholesale profit per car fell, and higher fuel prices and rapidly rising interest rates together cost an estimated $200 per unit.

takeaways.title: Profit nearly doubled, despite a debt charge
takeaways.text: Consolidated net income was $483M, up from $263M a year ago — a 6.0% net margin. Of it, $194M belongs to noncontrolling interests, leaving $289M for Carvana Co. shareholders ($0.39 diluted EPS per Class A share, vs $0.21). The quarter absorbed a $53M charge for retiring debt early; a year ago it absorbed a $120M warrant charge.

oneTimers: Below operating income sits a $53M loss on debt extinguishment — the cost of redeeming Carvana's Senior Secured Notes due 2030 early, including writing off related issuance costs. It is a financing one-off, not a cost of selling cars.

Other expense, net of $11M is also mostly one-off in nature: it mainly reflects derecognising the original Root warrants in the 2026 Warrant Exchange and a $5M fall in the value of the new warrants, partly offset by a $7M gain on its beneficial interests in securitizations.
footerNote: The flow uses consolidated net income of $483M, as reported, so the figures tie exactly. Cost of revenue is the statement's cost of sales.
